53784-old-melbourne-memories-second-edit.creator: Rolf Boldrewood
53784-old-melbourne-memories-second-edit.description: A book by Rolf Boldrewood. t, at the intersection of Elizabeth and Flinders Streets, one instinctively remarks the long crowded suburban trains, laden with homeward-bound passengers, quitting the city and care for the night's charmed interval. All the streets of busy Melbourne are yet thronged, in spite of the apparently rapid diminution which is proceeding.

arxiv-2207-03914.title: The Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope: Key science drivers
arxiv-2207-03914.creator: Joanna Ramasawmy, Pamela D. Klaassen, Claudia Cicone, Tony K. Mroczkowski, Chian-Chou Chen, Thomas Cornish, Elisabete da Cunha, Evanthia Hatziminaoglou, Doug Johnstone, Daizhong Liu, Yvette Perrott, Alice Schimek, Thomas Stanke, Sven Wedemeyer
arxiv-2207-03914.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joanna Ramasawmy, Pamela D. Klaassen, Claudia Cicone, Tony K. Mroczkowski, Chian-Chou Chen, Thomas Cornish, Elisabete da Cunha, Evanthia Hatziminaoglou, Doug Johnstone, Daizhong Liu, Yvette Perrott, Alice Schimek, Thomas Stanke, Sven Wedemeyer. The Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope (AtLAST) is a concept for a 50m class single-dish telescope that will provide high sensitivity, fast mapping of the (sub-)millimeter sky.

arxiv-2212-11564.title: Elastic precursor effects during the Ba 1-x Sr x TiO 3 ferroelastic phase transitions
arxiv-2212-11564.creator: Francesco Cordero, Francesco Trequattrini, Paulo Sergio da Silva Jr, Michel Venet, Oktay Aktas, Ekhard K. H. Salje
arxiv-2212-11564.description: Abstract Elastic softening in the paraelastic phases of Ba 1-x Sr x TiO 3 is largest near the transition temperatures and decreases on heating smoothly over extended temperature ranges. Softening extends to the highest measured temperature(850 K) for Ba-rich compounds.

arxiv-2401-15571.title: New results on sparse representations in unions of orthonormal bases
arxiv-2401-15571.creator: Tao Zhang, Gennian Ge
arxiv-2401-15571.description: Abstract The problem of sparse representation has significant applications in signal processing. The spark of a dictionary plays a crucial role in the study of sparse representation. Donoho and Elad initially explored the spark, and they provided a general lower bound.

arxiv-2407-10938.title: Comparing AI versus Optimization Workflows for Simulation-Based Inference of Spatial-Stochastic Systems
arxiv-2407-10938.creator: Michael A. Ramirez-Sierra
arxiv-2407-10938.description: Abstract Abstract Model parameter inference is a universal problem across science. This challenge is particularly pronounced in developmental biology, where faithful mechanistic descriptions require spatial-stochastic models with numerous parameters, yet quantitative empirical data often lack sufficient granularity due to experimental limitations.

arxiv-2505-23225.title: Generalizability vs. Counterfactual Explainability Trade-Off
arxiv-2505-23225.creator: Fabiano Veglianti, Flavio Giorgi, Fabrizio Silvestri, Gabriele Tolomei
arxiv-2505-23225.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the relationship between model generalization and counterfactual explainability in supervised learning. We introduce the notion of ε \varepsilon - valid counterfactual probability ( ε \varepsilon -VCP) – the probability of finding perturbations of a data point within its ε \varepsilon -neighborhood that result in a label change.

arxiv-2510-09469.title: Scalable Multi-Agent Path Finding using Collision-Aware Dynamic Alert Mask and a Hybrid Execution Strategy
arxiv-2510-09469.creator: Bharath Muppasani, Ritirupa Dey, Biplav Srivastava, Vignesh Narayanan
arxiv-2510-09469.description: Abstract Multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) remains a critical problem in robotics and autonomous systems, where agents must navigate shared spaces efficiently while avoiding conflicts. Traditional centralized algorithms that have global information, such as Conflict-Based Search (CBS), provide high-quality solutions but become computationally expensive in large-scale scenarios due to the combinatorial explosion of conflicts that need resolution.

pmc-11364439.title: Defining cell type-specific immune responses in a mouse model of allergic contact dermatitis by single-cell transcriptomics
pmc-11364439.creator: Youxi Liu, Meimei Yin, Xiaoting Mao, Shuai Wu, Shuangping Wei, Shujun Heng, Yichun Yang, Jinwen Huang, Zhuolin Guo, Chuan Li, Chao Ji, Liu Hu, Wenjie Liu, Ling-juan Zhang, Brian S Kim, Youxi Liu, Meimei Yin, Xiaoting Mao, Shuai Wu, Shuangping Wei, Shujun Heng, Yichun Yang, Jinwen Huang, Zhuolin Guo,
pmc-11364439.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD), a prevalent inflammatory skin disease, is elicited upon repeated skin contact with protein-reactive chemicals through a complex and poorly characterized cellular network between immune cells and skin resident cells. Here, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the murine hapten-elicited model of ACD reveals that upon elicitation of ACD, infiltrated CD4+ or CD8+ lymphocytes were primarily the IFNγ-producing type 1 central memory phenotype.

pmc-11365667.title: Efficacy and safety of therapeutic vaccines for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials update
pmc-11365667.creator: Mekuanint Geta, Getachew Mengistu, Endalew Yizengaw, Tsegahun Manyzewal, Asrat Hailu, Yimtubeznash Woldeamanuel
pmc-11365667.description: Background:Most people diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) need treatment to help reduce the risk of liver disease and limit disease transmission. Therapeutic vaccine (TV) candidates have been under study for their clinical effects on inducing HBV-specific host immune responses. This review aimed to systematically synthesize updated evidence on the efficacy and safety of TVs in patients with CHB.

pmc-11368141.title: Clinical Diagnostic Challenge in a Case of Disseminated Talaromyces marneffei Infection Misdiagnosed Initially as Pulmonary Tuberculosis: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-11368141.creator: Qiujing Li, Mingwu Li, Shuxian Wang, Alan F Geater, Jingyi Dai
pmc-11368141.description: This case reports a middle-aged male patient who was HIV-negative and initially misdiagnosed as pulmonary tuberculosis but was eventually diagnosed with disseminated Talaromyces marneffei (T. marneffei) infection by next-generation sequencing. The patient presented with respiratory symptoms, recurrent bone pain, and subcutaneous masses as the main symptoms.

pmc-11500329.title: Impact of dehulling, germination and fermentation on the bioactive and functional properties of grey pea flour
pmc-11500329.creator: Armaghan Amanipour, Yasaman Samaei, Olof Böök, Yvonne Granfeldt, Claudia E. Lazarte
pmc-11500329.description: IntroductionGrey pea is a largely overlooked legume in the Nordic countries, and its potential uses in various food products remain unexplored. It is a nutrient-rich crop with low environmental impact, making it an attractive option for sustainable and nutritious plant-based alternatives.

pmc-11574807.title: Protein profile of mouse endolymph suggests a role in controlling cochlear homeostasis
pmc-11574807.creator: Masatoshi Fukuda, Hiroki Okanishi, Daisuke Ino, Kazuya Ono, Takeru Ota, Eri Wakai, Takashi Sato, Yumi Ohta, Yoshiaki Kikkawa, Hidenori Inohara, Yoshikatsu Kanai, Hiroshi Hibino
pmc-11574807.description: SummaryThe cochlea contains two extracellular fluids, perilymph and endolymph. Endolymph exhibits high potential of approximately +80 to +110 mV (depending on species), which sensitizes sensory hair cells. Other properties of this unique fluid remain elusive, owing to its minuscule volume in rodent cochlea. We therefore developed a technique to collect high-purity endolymph from mouse cochleae.

pmc-12439084.title: Multi‐Millennial Genetic Resilience of Baltic Diatom Populations Disturbed in the Past Centuries
pmc-12439084.creator: Alexandra Schmidt, Sarah Bolius, Anna Chagas, Juliane Romahn, Jérôme Kaiser, Helge W. Arz, Miklós Bálint, Anke Kremp, Laura S. Epp
pmc-12439084.description: Little is known about the genetic diversity and stability of natural populations over millennial time scales, although the current biodiversity crisis calls for heightened understanding. Marine phytoplankton, the primary producers forming the basis of food webs in the oceans, play a pivotal role in maintaining marine ecosystems health and serve as indicators of environmental change.

pmc-12711599.description: The buffalo treehopper, Stictocephala bisonia (Kopp and Yonke, 1977), is an invasive pest originating from the United States and capable of causing severe damage to many plants. It is now established in many countries in the northern hemisphere and was first recorded in China in 2017. However, the origin of the S.

pmc-13066023.title: Computation and resource efficient genome-wide association analysis for large-scale imaging studies
pmc-13066023.creator: Zhiwen Jiang, Jason Stein, Tengfei Li, Ethan Fang, Yun Li, Patrick Sullivan, Hongtu Zhu
pmc-13066023.description: Imaging genetics links genetic variations to brain structures and functions, but the computational challenges posed by high-dimensional imaging and genetic data are significant. In voxel-level genome-wide association studies, we introduce a Representation learning-based Voxel-level Genetic Analysis (RVGA) framework that reduces computational time and storage burden by over 200 times.

pmc-13075953.title: Mapping adaptive immune responses toward fungal antigens in inflammatory bowel disease using T cell repertoire sequencing and phage-immunoprecipitation sequencing
pmc-13075953.creator: Aya K H Mahdy, Hesham ElAbd, Melanie Prinzensteiner, Hannah Jebens, Kostas Sivickis, Petra Bacher, Thomas Vogl, Mathilde Poyet, Andre Franke
pmc-13075953.description: Background and AimsImmune reactivity to the gut mycobiome has been implicated in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), particularly Crohn’s disease (CD), but the systemic adaptive immune repertoire targeting the gut mycobiome remains incompletely defined. We aimed to map systemic T cell and antibody responses to fungal antigens in IBD.

pmc-13081583.title: Effects of perioperative probiotic supplementation on postoperative gastrointestinal recovery in elderly hip fracture patients: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13081583.creator: Lingjing Liu, Naiyuan Tian, Yu Sun, Shuting Ren, Lingying Liu, Qun Xie, Hui Zheng, Mengmeng Li
pmc-13081583.description: BackgroundEnhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol aims to accelerate recovery and reduce complications in postoperative patients. Preoperative carbohydrate intake is recommended to reduce insulin resistance but is limited by safety concerns in elderly trauma patients. Probiotics may improve gastrointestinal function and barrier integrity.

pmc-13370270.title: Synergistic adsorption mechanisms in a multifunctional BAC-GO-rGO hybrid nanostructure for the enhanced removal of Ni2+ and methylene blue
pmc-13370270.creator: Sankalpa Perera, Sanduni Dabare, Imalka Munaweera, Saranga Diyabalanage
pmc-13370270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rising levels of industrial effluent containing heavy metals, including Ni2+ and cationic dyes such as methylene blue (MB), pose significant threats in terms of toxicity, stability, and bioaccumulation in ecological food chains. This study focuses on developing an efficient ternary BAC-GO-rGO composite with an optimized weight ratio of 80 : 15 : 5 for activated carbon, graphene oxide (GO), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO), respectively.

pmc-13566033.title: Anterior Segment Complications After Radiotherapy for Sinonasal and Nasopharyngeal Cancer: High Frequency in Maxillary Sinus Cancer Treated with RADPLAT
pmc-13566033.creator: Mutsumi Koyama, Seika Den, Akinori Baba, Hirokazu Ashida, Masao Kobayashi, Tadashi Nakano
pmc-13566033.description: Objectives: To characterize the frequency and temporal patterns of anterior segment findings after radiotherapy for sinonasal and nasopharyngeal cancer, with particular focus on anterior segment neovascularization and its association with superselective intra-arterial cisplatin infusion with concurrent radiotherapy (RADPLAT). Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 113 patients treated with intensity-modulated radiotherapy between 2019 and 2022.
